subject.title: fix(backup): sweep stale temp artifacts before creating new backup

question: Should `backup create` automatically delete OpenClaw-owned stale staging dirs and archive temps after the grace window once the timestamped-output gap is fixed?
rationale: The code repair is mechanical, but the destructive cleanup policy changes what old partial backup artifacts mean for operators and should be accepted by an owner before merge.

options.title: Accept guarded cleanup after repair
options.body: Fix the timestamped basename gap, keep the one-hour owner-guarded startup sweep, and merge after focused tests and real terminal proof.

options.title: Narrow cleanup scope
options.body: Limit cleanup to a smaller class of artifacts, such as only owner-marked artifacts, accepting that pre-PR orphan cleanup remains incomplete.

options.title: Pause the PR
options.body: Do not merge startup deletion until maintainers choose a different recovery or external janitor policy.

recommendation.title: Accept guarded cleanup after repair
recommendation.body: Fix the timestamped basename gap, keep the one-hour owner-guarded startup sweep, and merge after focused tests and real terminal proof.

likelyOwner.reason: This handle merged the related memory stale-temp cleanup precedent and has recent backup test-area history, making them a reasonable routing candidate for the cleanup-risk decision.
